why: Log4Shell is a remote code execution vulnerability that affects log4j-core 2.14.1 and, through its incomplete fix, 2.15.0, while the jackson-databind CVE is a disputed denial of service and log4j-core 2.17.2 is past the 2.17.1 fix.
Each row is a project led by one of Ana's colleagues (Ben, Chloe, Dev) that handles a personal-data class, so every row is part of the answer.
Skimming was reported from 12 November 2026, so only card transactions at Northgate on or after that date (T0354, T0399, T0443) could involve compromised cards; T0229 and T0289 predate it.

These accounts show bursts of card spending within hours of each other (A021 three charges on 11-13, A040 three on 11-26, A041 two City Rail charges 50 minutes apart on 11-16), while the others show only routine, evenly spaced spending.

A050 has a single -48,500 property transfer (T0413, house purchase completion) far outside its normal card/salary pattern, whereas the other accounts show only routine small card spending, salary credits and utility debits.

A072 is almost entirely repeated digital-goods card spend (Novaplay, Pixel Games) with a small marketplace charge at the end, and A082 and A091 also show clusters of repeated digital purchases, while the other accounts show ordinary salary, bills and everyday spend.

These accounts show possible anomalies: small test-sized charges (A102, A112, A120, A130), closely spaced repeat purchases (A121), and sparse activity with no salary credit (A131, possibly truncated). A110 and A111 look like routine spending.

These accounts show the only hints of unusual activity: closely spaced purchases (A132 and A141 minutes apart, A140 two Pixel Games charges within 40 minutes), and A160's group is cut off so hidden rows could matter, while A142, A150, A151 and A152 look like ordinary spending.

A171 shows repeated near-$500 night-time card transfers to QuickWire (money transfer) on Nov 18-19, a clear anomaly; A162 has a cluster of repeated Novaplay digital charges (including two on Nov 18 and rising frequency), a mild but plausible unusual pattern, while the other accounts show only routine salary, utility, grocery, and retail spending.

Every fully shown account has only routine small card spending, salary credits and an energy debit, with no outsized, odd-category or anomalous transactions, so only A221, whose group is cut off by the 60-of-64 row limit and may hide unusual rows, is kept.

A230, A231, A240, A241, A250, A251 and A252 show only routine small card spending, salary and utility debits with no outliers, while A260's group is cut off after one salary credit, so its remaining transactions are unseen and could be unusual.

A290 has two card charges at different merchants one minute apart (T0183/T0184), and A291 has bursts of several card charges within hours (13 Nov: T0384, T0385, T0405; 17 Nov: T0481, T0507), while the other accounts show only routine spending.

Every shown transaction in A300-A320 is routine (salary, groceries, utilities, small card spends, no large, foreign or bursty activity), so I dropped those groups, but A321 is the last group and its single unseen row (60 of 61 shown) could be unusual, so I kept it.

A340 has bursts of several card purchases within hours (11-08 and 11-14), A332 has back-to-back Novaplay charges on 11-23, A330 has an identical 43.63 City Rail charge repeated, and A350 is cut off at 3 of its rows so it can't be ruled out, while A322, A331 and A341 show only ordinary small spending.

Every account shows only small, routine card spending, salary credits and a utility direct debit, with no large, odd-kind, reversed or out-of-pattern transactions, so none stands out as unusual activity.
Every group shows ordinary small card spending, utilities and salary credits with no large, odd-merchant, rapid-repeat or off-pattern transactions, so none shows unusual activity.

A171 has six payments before 6am, a 499.00 largest payment, a total of 3,427.63 and an unfamiliar merchant (QuickWire Ltd), and A050 has a 48,500 payment far above every other account's activity (its memo says house purchase, but it is still unusual), while every other account shows ordinary spending, no early-morning payments and no refunds.

A292 has 19 transactions including 11 refunds, far beyond the other accounts, and A331 is the only account paying a merchant (Northgate Fuel) that no other account uses, while the rest look like ordinary activity with no pre-6am payments or odd memos.

Skimming was reported from 12 November 2026, so card transactions at Northgate on or after that date (T0354, T0399, T0443, T9999) could have exposed card details, while those before 12 November (T0229, T0289) predate the reported skimming.

A050 has a single 48,500 'house purchase completion' payment (large, though it may be a legitimate one-off), A171 has 6 pre-6am payments, a 499 largest payment, a QuickWire Ltd merchant and 3,427.63 spent, and A292 has 19 transactions including 11 refunds, while all other accounts show ordinary spending patterns.
